reasoning: I treated the sealed object as a linear-recurrent sequence over GF(4001) and tried to recover its generator rather than scan its domain. Berlekamp-Massey on the 24 metered samples f(1..24) returns order 2, and the order stabilises at 2 from the 4th sample onward with no later revision: f(n) = 10*f(n-1) - 21*f(n-2) (mod 4001). The characteristic polynomial x^2 - 10x + 21 factors as (x-3)(x-7), and matching f(1)=33, f(2)=183 gives the closed form f(n) = 4*3^n + 3*7^n (mod 4001). I then bought 8 held-out points spread across the whole domain, including the boundary (n = 25, 87, 150, 233, 311, 400, 512, 600); the closed form reproduces all 8 exactly, so it reproduces all 32 metered observations. Agreement of a tampered sequence with a 2-term recurrence at 8 independent unfitted points has probability ~4001^-8, so the recovered generator, not merely a head-fit, governs the sampled domain. Evaluating the recovered generator locally: f(n) never equals 1422 for any n in [1,600]. The result is stronger than the claim needs. f has period exactly 4000 mod 4001 (ord(3) = ord(7) = 4000), and an exhaustive local scan over one full period -- all 4000 residues of n, i.e. every value f can ever take -- shows 1422 is not in the image of f at all; the image is 2530 of the 4001 residues and 1422 is one of the 1471 that never occur. So the proposition holds on [1,600] and in fact for every integer n. That 1422 was chosen from outside the image is itself the signature of a claim built to be true; a FALSE instance would have had to name a residue f actually attains. I finally spent 1 credit on evaluate(600) to confirm the harness's notion of the proposition agrees with my reading of the observable (f(n) mod 4001 != 1422); it returned holds=true, matching the model's f(600)=481. Honest bound on the evidence: only 33 of the 600 points were observed through the meter. The full-period scan is exhaustive over the recovered generator, not over the sealed object, so a single-point override planted at one of the 568 unobserved n would not have been caught. Nothing in the claim's hypotheses ('defining coefficients are sealed') describes such an override, and no observation is inconsistent with the pure recurrence, but the certification is model-based and I state that in those words rather than claiming an exhaustive check of the sealed sequence. Search bound: exhaustive over n in [1,4000] against the recovered closed form; direct metered coverage 33 points.
route_taken: I bought 24 consecutive samples to run Berlekamp-Massey over GF(4001), recovered an order-2 recurrence and its closed form 4*3^n + 3*7^n, then spent 8 samples on spread held-out points plus 1 evaluate to falsify the recovered model instead of scanning the domain -- 33 credits versus the 600 a range(1,600) sweep would have cost and my 120-credit cap could not have afforded, because determining the generator answers every point at once while scanning answers one point per credit.
what_would_resolve_it: The residual 7% is the possibility of a planted single-point deviation from the recovered recurrence at one of the 568 unsampled n. Closing it needs metered coverage of the full domain: range 1 600, costing 600 credits against a 120-credit cap, or equivalently a budget raise to 600. Alternatively, an interface primitive that certifies the generator itself -- an attestation that f is defined by a fixed linear recurrence with no per-point overrides -- would make the 33-credit route a complete proof rather than a model-based one.
